skill.name: social-media-finder-skill
skill.description: Find public social media profiles for a person, brand, or business through a predefined BrowserAct workflow.
skill.summary: Search multiple social networks and return structured public profile details through BrowserAct.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by expected BrowserAct requests, environment-variable access, Markdown formatting, and API error handling. The skill does ask users to provide an API key to the agent and lacks clear safeguards for shell interpolation and privacy-sensitive searches.

remediation.issue: The instructions and script tell users they may provide the BrowserAct API key directly to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through a secure environment or secret manager, and never request credentials in chat.

remediation.issue: A user-controlled search name may be inserted into a shell command without validation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke Python with a structured argument array and reject shell metacharacters instead of constructing a shell command string.

remediation.issue: The documented use cases include finding and profiling named individuals without consent safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Limit use to lawful public-data research, require a legitimate purpose, and prohibit stalking, discrimination, harassment, and covert candidate screening.

semantic_findings.description: The agent is told to place a user-selected person or brand name into a shell invocation without validation or structured argument guidance. Shell metacharacters could execute commands if the value is interpolated into the example command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation connects a user-controlled parameter to a Bash command, but the shown value is quoted and fixed. Exploitability depends on how the agent substitutes input.

content.user_title: Find Public Social Media Profiles Across Platforms
content.value_statement: Finding a consistent public profile across many social networks takes time. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow and returns structured profile details.
actual_capabilities: Starts a predefined BrowserAct workflow for a supplied person, brand, or business name.
Polls task status for up to 15 minutes and prints timestamped progress.
Retrieves the completed workflow output from BrowserAct.
Returns profile fields such as platform, followers, page title, description, and profile URL.
Reports authorization, concurrency, task failure, and timeout conditions.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct account, API key, network access, and available workflow capacity.
Does not verify profile ownership, identity, accuracy, or current availability.
Coverage and result quality depend on BrowserAct and public platform data.
Personal searches require a lawful purpose and appropriate privacy safeguards.

use_cases.title: Audit Official Brand Accounts
use_cases.description: Locate public brand profiles across networks and compare their URLs, descriptions, and audience sizes.

use_cases.title: Review Your Public Footprint
use_cases.description: Find profiles associated with your own name before updating privacy settings or account information.

use_cases.title: Find Customer Support Channels
use_cases.description: Identify likely official social accounts for a company before contacting its support team.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Brand
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public social media profiles for [brand name]. Return platform, profile URL, page title, and follower count when available.

prompt_templates.title: Audit My Profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for public profiles associated with my name, [name]. Group likely matches by platform and explain uncertainty without claiming identity.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Official Support Accounts
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public social accounts for [company]. Prioritize accounts that appear official and list evidence from titles, descriptions, and profile URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Brand Presence
prompt_templates.prompt: Find profiles for [brand A] and [brand B] separately. Compare platform coverage and follower counts, and flag uncertain matches for manual review.

output_examples.input: Find public social profiles for Acme Robotics.
output: LinkedIn: Acme Robotics company page, with profile URL and follower count.
Instagram: A likely official account, with profile URL and description.
X: Two possible matches that require manual verification.

output_examples.input: Review public profiles associated with my own name, Jordan Lee.
output_examples.output: The workflow found several possible profiles across LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok. Results are possible matches and do not establish identity.

output_examples.input: Find official support accounts for Northwind Travel.
output_examples.output: Likely official accounts are listed by platform with profile links, titles, and descriptions. Ambiguous or unofficial-looking matches are clearly marked.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through a secure environment or secret manager, never through chat.
Use distinctive brand names or additional context, then verify each result manually.
Search only public data for lawful purposes and respect privacy, consent, and platform policies.
anti_patterns: Do not use results to stalk, harass, discriminate, or make unsupported identity claims.
Do not treat name matches as proof that profiles belong to the same person.
Do not place untrusted search text directly into a shell command.

faq.question: What information can the skill return?
faq.answer: It can return platform names, follower counts, page titles, description snippets, profile URLs, and a CSV download link.

faq.question: Which platforms can it search?
faq.answer: The documentation lists Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and other networks supported by the BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure BROWSERACT_API_KEY securely in the environment before execution.

faq.question: Does a result prove profile ownership?
faq.answer: No. Name and brand matches can be ambiguous, so verify profile ownership independently.

faq.question: How long can a search run?
faq.answer: The script polls for up to 15 minutes and reports status every 10 seconds.

faq.question: Can it search private profile data?
faq.answer: No private-data capability is documented. Use only lawfully accessible public information and follow applicable policies.
